tb21_profile.skill: Write an interpreter for a language whose exact semantics must be reverse-engineered from a reference implementation (interp.py) - s-expression reading, environments, closures, special forms, stdin plumbing - and write it in that same language so it can evaluate itself
tb21_profile.domain: Programming-language implementation: Scheme/Lisp, parsers and evaluators, ASTs, closures and environments, stdin/stdout stream plumbing
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec at the deep end: build a self-hosting evaluator that must pass the reference's own test programs and then bootstrap on itself

searches: tools.py search tmax "expression evaluator|expression parser|recursive descent|stack machine|bytecode|virtual machine"

TMax-15K.reason: Reverse-engineer a stack language from a reference binary and reimplement it natively, matching stdout and error behaviour exactly on thousands of random programs.
Write an emulator for a written language spec (stack, opcodes, underflow error) plus run/test drivers; implement-a-language-from-spec at comparable depth.
Build a Go interpreter that parses and evaluates a custom mathematical DSL and orchestrates other components; full parse-then-evaluate pipeline.
Implement a small virtual machine in C that evaluates expressions encoded in a custom bytecode, working strictly from the written specification.
Build a custom bytecode emulator in Python: decode instructions, maintain machine state, produce exactly the specified output.
Write a Go interpreter that parses and evaluates a rule grammar with operators and boolean connectives; grammar-to-semantics in one piece.
Fix a C interpreter for a custom dependency language and make it evaluate a DAG to the right value; debugging evaluation order in an interpreter.
Write a real expression parser (recursive descent or shunting-yard) and evaluator instead of eval; the core parse/eval loop in miniature.
Repair a broken C stack-based virtual machine project until it builds and runs; reading someone else's evaluator and making its semantics right.
Analyse a stripped reference binary and write a program that is behaviourally equivalent; the 'match the reference implementation exactly' half of the TB task.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Two Brainfuck interpreter implementations plus a test program: compare and repair an interpreter until it runs the program correctly.
Read the C sources of a Lisp interpreter (Lispy) to work out how to build it, then drive it from the command line.
Write Lisp for a custom Lisp interpreter to solve an arithmetic problem; hands-on s-expression authoring against an unfamiliar dialect.
Same custom-Lisp-interpreter family: read the data file, express the computation in the dialect the interpreter accepts.
Implement my-last in Clojure without the builtin: recursive list traversal in a Lisp, exactly what a metacircular eval is built from.
Debug a buggy Clojure program that reads EDN config; reading and repairing s-expression source in a Lisp dialect.
Use the custom Lisp interpreter at bin/lisp over a data file; more exposure to writing and running Lisp, lighter reasoning.
Find a .lisp data file and use the Lisp interpreter to compute the missing value; Lisp-dialect fluency, modest difficulty.
Babashka script defining two functions and composing them over CLI args; function definition and application in a Lisp, nothing deeper.
Drive an interactive tactic REPL to build a proof term; symbolic-term manipulation through a line-oriented interpreter.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Feed a Lisp interpreter s-expressions exercising head/tail, nested lists, import and recursion; the exact language shape eval.scm must handle.
Prefix-notation calculator reading nested expressions line-by-line from stdin; the same recursive prefix-form evaluation and stdin plumbing.
Lex source into tokens and run them through a real Parser, inspecting results in a REPL; front-end of an interpreter in practice.
Build a whole programming language (Octaspire Dern) from source and drive its REPL; language-implementation codebase familiarity.
Write and run an R6RS Scheme program under a Scheme package manager; actual Scheme authoring, the output language of the TB task.
Static-analysis pass over a Brainfuck interpreter written in C; reading interpreter source closely enough to reason about its defects.
Define a new Forth word implementing Newton's method; programming in a stack language by composing words, close to writing eval primitives.
Gforth program converting an integer to its decimal string; low-level manipulation inside a minimal language runtime.
Script that repeatedly reads one line from stdin, decodes it and loops; the line-at-a-time stdin protocol eval.scm must implement.
A REPL that supports importing packages at runtime; dynamic evaluation of user input inside a running interpreter.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: NodeVisitor.visit/generic_visit broken in a PEG parser: fixing the tree-walking dispatch that every evaluator is built around.
Nested-structure parsing (parentheses, brackets) broken; reading balanced nested parens is literally the s-expression reader.
Tokenizer emits wrong token types for identifiers; getting the lexer's token classification right is step one of eval.
Tokenizer fails on strings and identifiers with unusual characters; edge-case handling in a real language front end.
Custom rule callbacks with the wrong arity in a grammar engine; wiring user-supplied functions into the evaluation walk.
Recursion error on deeply nested brackets; exactly the failure a naive recursive reader hits, and a metacircular eval nests three deep.
Grammar.as_rule renders rules incorrectly; round-tripping a grammar back to its source form, a self-description problem.
Missing Token.is_child_of after a refactor; navigating a parse tree's parent/child structure.
Bug in a hand-written recursive-descent TOML parser; same class of character-at-a-time parsing code.
Regex for a tag pattern is missing parentheses, corrupting parse results; grouping errors in a parser's pattern definitions.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Boolean short-circuiting must lazily resolve variable references so an unresolved name never errors: evaluation-order semantics in an interpreter.
Chained assignment a = b = c unsupported in an interpreter; implementing an assignment form correctly in the evaluator.
Add a missing builtin (Memcmp) to an interpreter so scripts that call it work; extending a primitive set to match a reference implementation.
Enums and the parse hook interact wrongly; getting a language construct's evaluation to match the reference tool's behaviour.
A name lookup takes a different code path that mishandles implicit arrays: environment/lookup semantics inside an interpreter.
AST transformation governing what a restricted eval permits; direct work on compile-and-evaluate machinery.
Implicit array handling in the same template interpreter; more evaluator-semantics debugging against a reference implementation.
Assigning a list to another variable must alias, not copy; getting reference vs value semantics right in a language translator.
Type inference fails on inhomogeneous tuples indexed non-constantly; semantic-analysis stage of a compiler.
Another semantic-stage defect in the same Python-to-C/Fortran translator; compiler-frontend reasoning, different specific construct.

final_top10.reason: Reverse-engineer a language from its reference implementation and reimplement it so outputs and errors match exactly on random programs.
Implement a whole small language from its written spec, including error behaviour, plus the scripts that run and test it.
Make short-circuit evaluation resolve variables lazily so the interpreter matches the reference tool; evaluation-order semantics.
Exercises a Lisp interpreter over nested s-expressions, head/tail, import and recursion: the exact language shape eval.scm must cover.
Fix the visit/generic_visit dispatch in a PEG parser: the tree-walking dispatch every evaluator, metacircular or not, is built on.
Write an interpreter that parses a custom mathematical language and evaluates it as part of a larger pipeline.
Implement chained assignment in an interpreter so a = b = c evaluates like the reference; adding a special form correctly.
Build a virtual machine in C that evaluates expressions in a custom encoding, working only from the written specification.
Prefix-notation evaluator reading nested expressions one line at a time from stdin: same recursive form and same I/O protocol.
Two Brainfuck interpreter implementations and a test program: diff and repair an interpreter until it runs the program correctly.

notes: Retrieval was badly off here - the shortlist surfaced RPN calculators, GCD-in-ARM64 and tqdm progress bars. Nearly every candidate I kept came from my own searches. The strongest transfer in the whole pool is SWE-Rebench's d0c-s4vage/pfp cluster: pfp is an interpreter for 010-Editor template scripts, and its issues are pure evaluator semantics (chained assignment, lazy short-circuit variable resolution, missing builtins) measured against a reference implementation - which is exactly this task's relationship to interp.py. That is unusual for SWE-Rebench, so its scores here are genuinely high rather than inflated. TMax's stack-machine / bytecode-VM / DSL-interpreter family is deep and I could have filled 20 slots; task_001481_3bacc41d is the single best item in the pool because it also demands byte-exact agreement with the reference. No corpus contains a Scheme or metacircular task - the only true Scheme items are tw_165299 (write an R6RS program) and RTS's Lispy/Clojure families, which give dialect fluency but no interpreter construction. Self-application (an evaluator running itself) has no analogue anywhere in the pool; I did not pretend otherwise. RTS's custom-Lisp-interpreter family has ~10 near-identical variants - dedupe at merge.
